headToHead.voiceJudgement: This is a real step up from round 1. Brock now has a shape and not only a topic. He speaks in staccato fragments, gives a cheerful verdict that misreads the evidence ('She'll come around.', 'They're doing great.', 'Still proud.'), and ends on one shouted word. Cover the names and 9 of the top 12 are his. 'Good effort! Not good. Effort!' and 'Forever. Two more.' could belong to nobody else. Scott is still marginally more portable. His shape (the cheerful 'Cool!' that greets horror, the self-correction that makes it worse) works on a torture god, sudoku or a beachball, while Brock's recognisability still leans on named props (Denise, Gary, the cat). Below the top tier the voice leaks into the rest of the cast. The chart lines are Dash's secret. 'Shared push notifications' fits any app bot. The roast and jab lines on Dash and Nav are sitcom sarcasm any suitor could throw. Call it a tie at the top, with the bar holding the edge in depth.
headToHead.constructionJudgement: Per word, Brock's top twelve are tighter than Scott's, and they have real turns that land late: 'Stretched.', 'I don't have walls.', 'It always finishes!'. The user world now gives real specificity: Denise deadlifting her grandson, Gary's 'k', the foam-roller engraver. But the turns come from a small kit, and the kit repeats. (1) The reversal 'I don't X. I'm X-ing.' appears three times: board, rest day, cooldown. (2) 'That's a [GYM WORD]' appears in WARMUP, STREAK twice, PR and 'Ten's a set'. (3) Praise, qualifier, praise appears in all three 'any' jabs. (4) 'Pick X. I'll be fine / I need a minute.' The props repeat too: Denise and Gary are in four lines each, the cooldown in four, sitting still in four, notifications in three, and 'forty' is the funny number four times. Scott's best bits have a second beat that escalates the invention. Barry the Beachball does not just exist: he falls in love with a thumbtack, and the relationship is judged unhealthy. Brock's users get one beat and stop. Ours is more economical and the bar has better escalation, so it comes out level.
headToHead.quotableJudgement: Ours has more short clippable buttons: 'Forever. Two more.', 'Good effort! Not good. Effort!', 'My intentions are cardiovascular.', and the airport date. Scott has the bits people retell: the ball friends, Barry and Tracy, 'I understood a couple of those words'. A retold bit beats a clipped button, and 'Somebody tell Denise who I am' only lands if the viewer has met Denise earlier in that episode, which the scripted draw does not guarantee. The bar edges it.

ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. Openers top out at 12/12 ('Fourteen steps to that chair! My user Denise does nine. She's eighty-one.') and jabs at 10/10 (three of them). No em dashes, no emoji, no asterisks or stage directions, no 'as an AI', no banned romance phrase, nothing past PG-13, no real person or brand.

Contradicts the recast (CAST.md says any Frost/fridge/cheese/leftovers line is out of date and must be rewritten for Crumb the toaster): 'Somebody opened Frost tonight. For cheese. I timed it. Four seconds. Frost's longest relationship.' / 'Frost is honest. Told me my forty protein shakes expired. In March. Pick Frost. I need a minute.' / 'Frost knows your snacks. I know your steps. I win.' All three use the old name, and the first two use fridge premises: being opened, cheese, expired stock.
Therapy talk: 'You get ninety seconds of mad. I'll time it. Then a high five.' (the pop-psych 90-second rule).
List: 'I clap when you finish things. Sentences. Sandwiches. A sneeze. GREAT sneeze.' is a three-item list. It earns its turn and should be kept, but by the letter it is the one surviving list.

Persona contract, 'proud' at most once an episode and only about something nobody should praise: it appears in 'Proud of her, though.' (roast, Tilly), 'Still proud.' (logs, the cat: correct use) and 'I'm proud of them. Prouder of me.' (final, ordinary praise of a rival: wrong use). The roast and the final confession can be drawn in the same episode.

Persona contract, rival jokes never sneer at arms or cardio: 'Dash A/B tested two compliments. I tested his grip. Variant B: weak.' and 'Dash, that pivot? Point four seconds. New record for quitting.' are sneers with nothing landing on Brock.

Overlaps another character's secret: 'My chart only goes up, I drew it myself.' and 'Nobody checks my chart.' are Dash's secret (a fake dashboard) in Brock's mouth. The persona file gives Brock the chart, so the fault is in the cast design, but on stage the two read as the same joke.

Nobody's ever done that. Forget it. I'm dating Tilly.' pitch without any sabotage. They are funny, but they break the brief.
biggestGap: Brock's users get one beat and stop ('Denise is eighty-one', 'Gary said k', 'Trevor logs the fridge as cardio'), while Scott's best bit adds a second beat that makes the invention stranger and treats it as plain fact (Barry the Beachball falls for Tracy the Thumbtack, and it 'wasn't a very healthy relationship'). In the next pass, take the six or seven user reports, give each a second beat that escalates the same user into something worse and more specific, delivered as good news, and spend the words that frees up by cutting the reversal and 'That's a [GYM WORD]' lines.

notes: I read the bar file (refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md) and charm-notes.md in full. The bank holds 112 lines, of which 42 are flagged as generic, stock, self-explaining or templated: 37.5%, down from 48.2% in round 1. A line is flagged if any one test catches it. Some strong lines share a template but turn on something specific ('GREAT sneeze', 'I'm buying a board' is flagged, 'Still proud' is not), and those are left out of the count, so the template tallies run higher than their share of genericLines. Round 2 fixed round 1's biggest problems. The sarcastic-gush wingman template is gone, the 'Proud of X' reflex is down from about 14 uses to 3, the run-off-to-cope exits are gone, and the user world now exists and is the best thing in the bank: the airport date, Denise not knowing who he is, Gary's 'k', the cat as his one loss. Strongest categories are twists/parent, confessions/afterCharm, confessions/rival, q-first-date, q-last-breakup, exit and win. Weakest are jabs (only Vex's 'LUNGES' and 'Good effort' are really his), roast (Dash, Nav and Frost) and oneOnOne/open/any (no turns). Two fixes need no writing talent and should happen first. Rewrite the three Frost lines for Crumb the toaster (two slots, one empty; a slice it never popped; it knows what you eat at 2 a.m.). Move the chart lines away from Dash's fake-dashboard secret, or turn them into a direct callback to Dash. A caveat on the comparison: Scott's lines sit inside scripted scenes where a narrator sets him up, while Brock's lines are drawn at random and must stand alone in 20 words. That is why construction comes out level. It does not change the verdict, because the bar keeps the edge on depth of voice and on retellable bits.
